pb-01.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: Python is the most popular programming language in the world. People use it to build websites and bots, analyse data, automate routine work and create AI.
pb-01.lessons.0.blocks.1.html:
• Python developers are paid well — it is one of the most in-demand professions
  • The code reads almost like English
  • You will write your first program within five minutes
pb-01.lessons.0.blocks.2.html: This is what Python code looks like — try running it right here:
pb-01.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: On this site Python runs inside your browser, but for real work you need Python on your computer:
pb-01.lessons.1.blocks.1.html:
1. Go to python.org/downloads and download the latest version
  2. Run the installer
  3. ⚠️ Make sure to tick «Add Python to PATH» — this is the single most common beginner mistake!
  4. Click Install Now
pb-01.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: To verify: open a terminal (Win+R → cmd) and type:
pb-01.lessons.2.blocks.0.html: An editor (IDE) is a smart text editor: it highlights errors, completes your code and runs programs with one button.
pb-01.lessons.2.blocks.1.html:
1. Download the free VS Code from code.visualstudio.com (the one your mentor recommended)
  2. Install it and add the Python extension
  3. Create a file: main.py
  4. Run it: the ▶ button or F5
pb-01.lessons.2.blocks.2.html: Done — your workspace is ready. Now for the code itself.
pb-01.lessons.3.blocks.0.html: The print() function displays text on screen. Text goes inside quotes — double or single, it makes no difference:
pb-01.lessons.3.blocks.2.html: Notice: print() can output several things separated by commas, and numbers are written without quotes — Python computes them for you.
pb-01.lessons.3.blocks.3.html: Comments start with # — Python ignores them, they exist for humans:
pb-01.lessons.4.blocks.0.html: PyQuest is a game. The rules are simple:
pb-01.lessons.4.blocks.1.html:
• Theory — short cards with examples you can actually run
  • Quiz — check your understanding (70%+ required)
  • Tasks — write real code with automatic checking
  • Exam — a timed test. Pass it and the next level unlocks!
pb-01.lessons.4.blocks.2.html: Everything earns you XP — climb from Novice to Sensei. Study every day so you keep your streak. Let's go!
pb-01.quiz.0.q: Which function prints text to the screen?
pb-01.quiz.0.explain: In Python text is printed with the print() function.
pb-01.quiz.1.q: Which checkbox MUST be ticked when installing Python on Windows?
pb-01.quiz.1.explain: Without «Add Python to PATH» the python command will not work in the terminal.
pb-01.quiz.2.explain: Text in quotes is printed as is. To compute it, write it without quotes: print(5 + 5).
pb-01.quiz.3.q: How does a comment start in Python?
pb-01.quiz.3.explain: Comments in Python start with the # character.
pb-01.quiz.4.explain: VS Code is an editor (IDE) — a program that makes writing and running code comfortable.
pb-01.quiz.5.explain: Numbers without quotes get computed by Python: 3 + 4 = 7.
pb-01.tasks.0.hint: Use print("Привет, Python!") — the text must match exactly, including the exclamation mark.
pb-01.tasks.1.desc:
Print three lines:

Меня зовут Азиз
Я учу Python
День 1 из 14
pb-01.tasks.1.hint: Each print() outputs text on a new line. You need three print() calls.
pb-01.tasks.2.desc: Print the result of 25 * 4 (the number itself, not the text).
pb-01.tasks.2.hint: print(25 * 4) — no quotes! In quotes Python prints text, without them it does the maths.
pb-01.exam.tasks.0.desc:
Print two lines:

Я сдаю первый экзамен
Python - мой
pb-02.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: A variable is a name bound to a value. You create it with the = sign:
pb-02.lessons.0.blocks.2.html: The value can change at any moment — that is why it is called a «variable»:
pb-02.lessons.0.blocks.4.html: Naming rules: letters, digits and _ only; never start with a digit; case matters (Name and name differ). Give names meaning: user_age, not x.
pb-02.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: int is whole numbers, float is decimals (with a point). All maths operations work with them:
pb-02.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: Remember: plain division / always yields a float (7 / 2 = 3.5), while // drops the fractional part (7 // 2 = 3). The remainder % is very handy: evenness is checked as n % 2 == 0.
pb-02.lessons.2.blocks.0.html: A string is any text in quotes. Strings can be added (concatenated) and multiplied:
pb-02.lessons.3.blocks.0.html: An f-string is the most convenient way to put a variable inside text. Put f before the quotes and variables in curly braces:
pb-02.lessons.3.blocks.2.html: Inside {} you can write any expression — Python evaluates it. This is used constantly, so learn it well!
pb-02.lessons.4.blocks.0.html: Every value has a type. You can find it with the type() function:
pb-02.lessons.4.blocks.2.html: bool is the logical type: only True or False. Types can be converted:
pb-02.lessons.5.blocks.0.html: input() pauses the program and waits for the user to type. The result is always a string:
pb-02.lessons.5.blocks.2.html: ⚠️ The main trap: if you need an age or a number — wrap it in int():
pb-02.lessons.5.blocks.4.html: In this site's tasks the input is supplied automatically — just use input() as usual.
pb-02.quiz.0.q: What is the type of the value 3.14?
pb-02.quiz.0.explain: Numbers with a decimal point are float.
pb-02.quiz.1.explain: x is a string, and strings are added by joining: «5» + «5» = «55».
pb-02.quiz.3.q: How do you correctly insert the variable name into a string?
pb-02.quiz.3.explain: You need the letter f before the quotes AND curly braces: f'Hello, {name}'.
pb-02.quiz.4.explain: input() always returns a string. Even if 25 was typed, it is the string «25». For a number you need int().
pb-02.quiz.5.explain: // is integer division: the fractional part is dropped, leaving 3.
pb-02.quiz.6.explain: A variable name cannot start with a digit. 2players raises an error.
pb-02.tasks.0.desc: Create a variable name with the value "Азиз" and level with the value 5. Print with an f-string: Игрок Азиз, уровень 5
pb-02.tasks.1.desc: Use Python to compute how many seconds there are in a day (24 hours × 60 minutes × 60 seconds) and print the result as a single number.
pb-02.tasks.1.hint: print(24 * 60 * 60) — let Python do the maths, that is its strength!
pb-02.tasks.2.desc:
The program asks for a number via input() and then prints it doubled.

For example, with input 21 the output is 42

The input is supplied automatically during checking.
pb-02.tasks.2.hint: n = int(input(...)) — then n becomes a number and n * 2 is computed mathematically.
pb-02.exam.tasks.0.desc:
The program reads a name and then an age (as a number) via input(), and prints: Имя, через 10 лет тебе будет X

For example, for Тимур and 15: Тимур, через 10 лет тебе будет 25
pb-03.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: A list is an ordered collection of values in square brackets. It can hold anything:
pb-03.lessons.0.blocks.2.html: An empty list: items = [] — you can add elements to it later.
pb-03.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: Every element has a number — an index. ⚠️ Counting starts at zero!
pb-03.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: Negative indexes count from the end: [-1] is the last, [-2] the second to last. An element can be replaced:
pb-03.lessons.2.blocks.0.html: A slice cuts a piece out of a list: list[from:to]. The right boundary is not included:
pb-03.lessons.3.blocks.0.html: The main operations are add, insert and remove:
pb-03.lessons.4.blocks.0.html: Python can do the counting for you:
pb-03.lessons.4.blocks.2.html: The in operator checks whether an element is in the list:
pb-03.quiz.0.q: What is the index of the FIRST element of a list?
pb-03.quiz.0.explain: Indexing in Python starts at zero: the first element is [0].
pb-03.quiz.1.explain: [-1] is the last element, that is «z».
pb-03.quiz.2.explain: The slice [1:3] takes indexes 1 and 2 (the right boundary is excluded): [2, 3].
pb-03.quiz.3.q: How do you add an element to the END of a list?
pb-03.quiz.3.explain: append() adds to the end. insert(i, x) inserts by index; Python has no add/push.
pb-03.quiz.4.explain: len() is the number of elements — there are three.
pb-03.quiz.5.explain: remove(«b») deletes an element by value, leaving «a» and «c».
pb-03.quiz.6.q: How do you check whether 5 is in the list nums?
pb-03.quiz.6.explain: The in operator: the expression 5 in nums returns True or False.

  1. append "зелье"
  2. remove "камень"
  3. insert "меч" at the start (index 0)

Then print the resulting list.
pb-03.tasks.2.desc:
A list of damage over 5 hits is given. Print three lines:

Всего: 174
Макс: 70
Средний: 34.8
pb-03.exam.tasks.0.desc: A queue of players is given. The first player joined the server (remove them with pop(0)), and the player "Zeus" joined the end of the queue. Print the resulting list.
pb-04.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: Imagine you need to print «Hello» 100 times. Write 100 print lines? No! For repetition there are loops:
pb-04.lessons.0.blocks.2.html: Note the indentation (4 spaces): everything indented after the colon is the loop body, and it repeats. In Python indentation is not decoration, it is the law!
pb-04.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: range() creates a sequence of numbers. Three forms:
pb-04.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: Remember: range(n) goes from 0 to n-1 (the right boundary is excluded — just like slices). And end=' ' in print replaces the line break with a space.
pb-04.lessons.2.blocks.0.html: A for loop can walk through any list — element by element:
pb-04.lessons.2.blocks.2.html: If you need both the number and the element — use enumerate():
pb-04.lessons.3.blocks.0.html: A classic technique: create an accumulator variable before the loop and fill it inside:
pb-04.lessons.3.blocks.2.html: Shorthand: total += n is the same as total = total + n. Strings and lists accumulate the same way:
pb-04.lessons.4.blocks.0.html: break leaves the loop immediately. continue skips the current step and moves to the next:
pb-04.lessons.4.blocks.3.html: Nested loops are possible too — a loop inside a loop (for a multiplication table, say).
pb-04.quiz.0.q: How many times does the body of for i in range(3): run?
pb-04.quiz.1.explain: From 1 up to but not including 4: the numbers 1, 2, 3.
pb-04.quiz.3.explain: break aborts the loop entirely; the program continues after it.
pb-04.quiz.4.explain: A for loop also iterates strings — one letter at a time: к, у, б.
pb-04.quiz.5.q: Why does this code raise an error?
pb-04.quiz.5.explain: The loop body must be indented. Without indentation Python cannot tell what to repeat.
pb-04.quiz.6.explain: continue skips the rest of the loop body and moves to the next iteration.
pb-04.tasks.0.desc:
Print a countdown from 5 to 1, then the line Пуск!

5
4
3
2
1
Пуск!
pb-04.tasks.0.hint: for i in range(5, 0, -1): print(i) — and after the loop (not indented!) print("Пуск!")
pb-04.tasks.1.desc: Compute the sum of all numbers from 1 to 100 inclusive with a loop and print it. (Spoiler: it is 5050 — the problem Gauss solved in his head at seven!)
pb-04.tasks.1.hint: for n in range(1, 101): total += n. Note: 101, not 100 — the right boundary is excluded.
pb-04.tasks.2.desc:
A list of round scores is given. For each round print Раунд N: X очков (numbering from 1), and at the end Итого: сумма.

Раунд 1: 30 очков
Раунд 2: 45 очков
Раунд 3: 25 очков
Итого: 100
pb-04.tasks.2.hint: for i, score in enumerate(rounds, 1): print(f'Раунд {i}: {score} очков'), then print(f'Итого: {sum(rounds)}')
pb-04.exam.tasks.0.desc:
A list of numbers is given. Using a loop, collect only the even numbers (n % 2 == 0) into a new list evens and print it.

Expected output: [4, 8, 10]
pb-05.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: The if statement runs code only when the condition is true (True):
pb-05.lessons.0.blocks.2.html: As in loops: colon plus indentation. Everything indented runs conditionally; unindented lines always run.
pb-05.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: Conditions are built on comparisons. There are six:
pb-05.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: ⚠️ The most common beginner mistake: = assigns, == compares. In a condition it is always ==!
pb-05.lessons.2.blocks.0.html: else means «otherwise»: it runs when the condition is false. elif means «otherwise if»: checking several options in turn:
pb-05.lessons.2.blocks.2.html: Python goes top to bottom and runs the first matching branch, skipping the rest. That is why the order of conditions matters!
pb-05.lessons.4.blocks.2.html: An if can be nested inside another if (one more level of indentation):
pb-05.quiz.0.explain: == compares. A single = assigns a value to a variable.
pb-05.quiz.1.explain: 7 is not greater than 10 — the condition is false, so the else branch runs.
pb-05.quiz.2.explain: and requires BOTH conditions to be true.
pb-05.quiz.3.explain: The FIRST true branch runs: n >= 10 is True, and Python does not check the rest.
pb-05.quiz.4.explain: 5 > 3 is True, and not flips it: False.
pb-05.quiz.5.explain: For strings in checks for a substring: «ит» is inside «питон».
pb-05.quiz.6.q: How many elif branches can you write?
pb-05.quiz.6.explain: You can have as many elif branches as you like between if and else.
